lines: A single bathroom, and a good one: clean, a plant on the cistern, and a hand-lettered sign asking you kindly to jiggle the handle.
Anyone can use it. There is a hook for your coat, and the soap smells like lemons.
The other one, just the same, with a changing table folded against the wall and a stack of the good paper towels.
Whichever is free is yours.
A whole shelf of coffee makers, every kind there is: a glass pour-over, a stovetop moka pot, a siphon like something out of a science set, a percolator with a few decades on it.
They all still work, and most of them get used. It is a collection, not a museum.
The menu, in chalk: coffee every way you could want it, the Maple Smoke latte in a box of its own, and a row of paninis pressed to order — the kind you smell before you see.
Nothing on this board you would regret.

Bottles behind the right end of the counter: a cooler of beer from breweries an easy drive from here, and a few bottles of wine to take home, each with a little card in Ronnie's hand saying what it goes with.
Ask at the counter and one goes home with you. One of these evenings, one will.
A record player on the left wall, lid up, something warm and a little crackly turning on it.
Whoever is behind the counter picks the side. It is always the right one.
Crates of LPs, spread out so you can flip through them: jazz, old country, soul, and a few things nobody can quite place.
Every sleeve has been handled a hundred times, which is exactly what they are for.
The furniture is mid-century modern, all of it: low tables, tapered legs, chairs that look like they came off a magazine cover in 1958 and have been sat in happily ever since.
Nothing matches exactly, and it all goes together anyway.
A self-serve fridge up by the door: cold drinks, snacks, and ready-made dinners for anyone who would rather not cook tonight.
Help yourself, says the little sign on it. One of these weeks, you might.

people.name: Ronnie
lines: Morning. The board's right here — the Maple Smoke latte's the one everybody asks about.
That's my record on. Have a flip through the crates by the player if you like — there's always something good in there.
Take your time picking a table. The big doorway on the right goes straight through to 80 Main, and the bathrooms are up the hallway in the corner on the left — the steel door off it is the kitchen.
